Home/IoT Sensors/Medium precision triaxial tilt sensor

Triaxial tilt sensor.
Medium precision.
±0.1° accuracy.

H310-TS350M is a medium-precision triaxial tilt sensor with ±0.1° accuracy for racks, poles, fixed supports and machine frames. One-minute acquisition and four-hour scheduled reporting support regular inclination records across distributed assets. Choose the measured member and installation reference around the angle changes that matter to your project.

KEY FEATURES

Made for the way
you monitor.

Triaxial inclination monitoring with ±0.1° accuracy, one-minute acquisition and the connectivity selected for your installation.

±0.1° triaxial inclination

H310-TS350M combines the ±0.1° accuracy grade with X/Y/Z sensing. Define the reported angle channels and axis convention for your mounting arrangement.

One-minute acquisition

A one-minute acquisition interval provides frequent observations at the mounting point. Keep acquisition separate from the schedule for transmitting readings.

Four-hour scheduled reporting

A four-hour report schedule connects distributed measurements to Hitelecom Cloud or a compatible customer platform, using the selected radio and interface.

Protection for the installation

Choose a metal IP68 or plastic IP66 enclosure. The specified operating temperature is −40°C to +85°C; select the mounting kit for the measured member.

Commission with NFC

NFC activation and local configuration support installation and device commissioning. Record the asset ID, initial angle and orientation before monitoring.

An integration-ready project

Select 4G LTE, NB-IoT or LoRa by device variant. Agree the message fields and platform interface; remote firmware updates are available on supported versions.

A CLEARER VIEW OF CHANGE

Measure the angle.
Follow the trend.

H310-TS350M brings ±0.1° triaxial inclination monitoring to defined points on racks, poles, supports and equipment frames. Start with the angle change that needs review, then check the accuracy grade, mounting and environmental conditions. A clear installation reference makes readings from each point useful in a wider inspection programme.

    Define the point and orientation

    Fix the sensor to the selected member. Record its asset ID, bracket position, axis orientation and initial angle after installation.

  2. 02

    Match the grade to the change

    Assess the required angle change against ±0.1° accuracy. Specify the working range, reported increment and applicable test conditions for each reported channel.

  3. 03

    Give the history a purpose

    Assign review conditions and responsibilities. Validate readings, scheduled messages and the platform workflow using the completed installation.

ACQUISITION & REPORTING

Frequent sensing.
Scheduled reporting.

H310-TS350M acquires readings every minute and transmits scheduled reports every four hours. The datasheet states a 10-year reference operating profile at 25°C with normal signal conditions.

1 min

Acquisition interval

Frequent sensing at the installed monitoring point.

4 hours

Scheduled reporting

Six scheduled report intervals per day.

240

Acquisition cycles

Acquisition cycles between scheduled reports at this reference profile.

10 years*

Reference battery life

1-min acquisition, 4-hour reporting, 25°C and normal signal.

H310-TS350M · REFERENCE PROFILE1-minute acquisition.
4-hour scheduled reporting.

Actual battery life varies with enabled functions, event frequency and radio retries. Acquisition cycles do not specify how many individual samples a report contains or how long data are retained. Agree any event-reporting and notification requirements for the supplied configuration.

ANSWERS FOR YOUR PROJECT

Frequently
asked questions.

Practical answers for specifying, installing and integrating the H310-TS350M medium precision triaxial tilt sensor.

Ask about your project ↗
What is the H310-TS350M triaxial tilt sensor?+

H310-TS350M is a medium precision MEMS tilt sensor with ±0.1° accuracy and X/Y/Z sensing. It measures inclination at a defined mounting point, using the angle outputs and reference orientation specified by the supplied protocol.

Typical projects include warehouse rack uprights, poles, structural members and machine frames. One-minute acquisition and four-hour scheduled reporting support remote angle records for the selected points.

Explore the specification →
When should I choose H310-TS350M instead of H310-TS380C?+

Choose H310-TS350M when ±0.1° accuracy meets the monitoring objective. Where a finer measurement grade is required, review the H310-TS380C ±0.01° triaxial option.

Selection also depends on range, resolution, temperature, fixing stability and test conditions. Accuracy is separate from the displayed increment and the threshold that triggers a project review.

Compare the other triaxial grade →
How does a triaxial tilt sensor differ from a two-axis model?+

The triaxial version uses X/Y/Z sensing. The supplied protocol defines how those sensing axes are converted into reported angle channels and how the reference orientation is represented.

Choose the sensor around the outputs your monitoring plan needs and the mounting orientation. Three sensing axes alone do not establish three independent orientation angles or a complete 3D motion measurement.

Check the angle-output definition →
Does three-axis sensing measure yaw or compass heading?+

Gravity-referenced inclination does not independently determine yaw, which is rotation about the gravity direction. X/Y/Z labels identify the sensing axes; they should not be interpreted as a compass heading measurement.

For an application that needs heading or another motion quantity, describe it explicitly so the required sensing architecture can be reviewed before selection.

Discuss the required outputs →
How do I establish a reliable installation reference?+

Attach the sensor rigidly to the member whose inclination is to be monitored. Record the device ID, asset location, bracket position, axis orientation and initial angle after fixing.

Keep that reference with later readings. Recommission the reference after moving the device, changing the bracket or altering the measured member. A baseline supports comparison; it does not improve the stated accuracy.

See the measurement workflow →
What does the illustrated angle change represent?+

The example compares 0.3° at installation with 0.5° later, a +0.2° change in one reported inclination channel. It illustrates reference comparison, rather than a three-axis vector or a complete 3D orientation.

These example values do not define range, resolution, a minimum detectable change or a notification threshold. Set review conditions for the real mounting point and applicable measurement performance.

Review the example reading →
What are the acquisition and scheduled-reporting intervals?+

The reference profile acquires readings every minute and sends scheduled reports every four hours. This corresponds to 240 acquisition cycles between scheduled reports and six report intervals per day.

Acquisition frequency and transmission frequency are different. Agree which samples or values a report contains, any local retention, and the supported event-reporting and notification behaviour for your configuration.

Review the operating profile →
Under what conditions does the 10-year battery-life figure apply?+

The datasheet gives a 10-year reference with one-minute acquisition, four-hour reporting, 25°C and normal signal conditions. The battery configuration is 19000 mAh with a 38000 mAh option.

Actual service life varies with enabled functions, event frequency and radio retries. Select the power arrangement against the installation conditions and operating profile.

Check the reference conditions →
Which enclosure and environmental limits apply?+

The specified options are a metal IP68 enclosure or a plastic IP66 enclosure. Operating and storage temperature is −40°C to +85°C; operating humidity is 5% to 95% RH, non-condensing.

Select the enclosure, antenna and mounting kit for the actual exposure and access conditions. The 115 × 90 × 60 mm dimension is a platform body reference; verify the selected arrangement for installation drawings.

Review protection and mounting →
Can I choose 4G LTE, NB-IoT or LoRa?+

The datasheet lists LTE Cat.1 (4G), with NB-IoT and LoRa by selected variant. Choose the configuration around the installation country, regional bands, operator or compatible receiver, and the required data route.

LoRa identifies the radio option; a LoRaWAN requirement needs explicit protocol compatibility confirmation. Confirm the supplied radio, gateway and platform combination before ordering.

Plan the connection →
Can the readings be sent to our existing platform?+

Hitelecom Cloud or a compatible customer platform can be used with the supported data interface. Share your interface, authentication and asset-data requirements during the project review.

Agree a sample message that identifies the device, mounting point, channel names, axis convention, angle units, timestamps and reference. Test the complete path using the selected device configuration.

Review the data handover →
What are NFC and remote firmware updates used for?+

NFC activation and local configuration support installation and commissioning. Record the final settings and installation reference before starting the monitoring programme.

Remote firmware updates are supported on selected versions. Confirm availability and the supplied device configuration, together with your platform and update workflow.

Discuss commissioning requirements →
Can one triaxial model cover racks, structures, poles and machine frames?+

H310-TS350M can be evaluated across racks, poles, fixed supports, infrastructure members and machine frames where ±0.1° accuracy meets the monitoring objective. The Applications section covers tasks across nine sectors, with warehouse racking first.

For racks, identify uprights and fixing points; for infrastructure, define the monitored member with the responsible engineer. Machine-frame inclination is a static or settled-position task. Minute-interval tilt readings do not specify dynamic vibration, rapid motion or machinery alignment performance.

Explore the application tasks →
What information is needed for a quotation or OEM project?+

Include H310-TS350M, the installation country, quantities, application and rollout date. Share a site photograph or drawing, mounting orientation, required per-axis range, useful angle change and expected environment.

Add the selected network, platform interface, reporting and event-response requirements, sample acceptance criteria and any OEM / white-label needs. CE is completed for the H200/H300/H500 platform; confirm certificate applicability and other requested compliance references for the supplied configuration.

Prepare your project brief →
